subject: Sigma Commerce — proposed hosted commit step-up and rate cap recalibration
messages:
From: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv.mehta@sigma-commerce.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: priya@procurement.sigma-commerce.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted commit increase & short-term burst needs

Hi Dylan,

We had a couple of unexpectedly large Black Friday-like promotions in May and our hosted usage spiked well beyond the current committed band. Procurement wants us to lock in additional capacity for the rest of the year so we can stabilize cost and avoid throttles during campaigns.

Can Redwood propose:
- A monthly commit increase (looking at ~1.4x current commit) with a 3-month ramp rather than immediate billing step-up
- A small burst-pocket for campaign bursts (we expect maybe 10% of monthly tokens in a short window) with preferential overage rates
- Clear per-minute/per-second rate limits so our gateway can set backpressure correctly

We also need an updated mutual action plan and any paperwork for procurement. If pricing is favorable we can accelerate a signature.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Rajiv Mehta
Head of Platform Engineering
Sigma Commerce
rajiv.mehta@sigma-commerce.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv.mehta@sigma-commerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted commit increase & short-term burst needs

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the context and the clear asks. We can definitely support a staged commit increase plus a temporary burst pocket with explicit rate guidance so your gateway doesn't misinterpret backpressure.

Quick proposal (high level):
- Commit step: +40% monthly commit (effective over a 3-month ramp: 40% / 70% / 100% of the step on month 1/2/3) to smooth billing impact
- Burst pocket: 10% of monthly tokens reserved for campaign bursts; billed at a discounted overage rate (we're proposing 0.6x standard overage for burst consumption)
- Rate limits: add a per-minute token ceiling and a soft throttle rule (graceful 429s with KV-cache-preserved responses) — we'll provide recommended token/sec and token/min numbers based on your current seq length distribution
- Ops: we attach a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones (procurement review, security attestation, SSO/KMS notes) and a DocuSign-ready terms PDF

Next steps:
1) Ben/Monica: can you validate that the proposed discounting on burst overage (0.6x) and the 3-month ramp math are within allowed deal guardrails?
2) Rajiv: if that sounds reasonable, we'll drop in a short SOW and DocuSign link and set a single 30-minute kickoff to confirm onboarding and routing policies.

I've attached: Sigma_Mutual_Action_Plan_v2.xlsx and proposed-hosted-commit-terms-20270517.pdf

On a related note, if you want guaranteed throughput (zero shared throttles) we can show a Dedicated pool add-on quote, but the hosted commit + burst is usually the best mix for cost/latency for accounts at your scale.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com

Attachments:
- Sigma_Mutual_Action_Plan_v2.xlsx (MAP with milestones and timelines)
- proposed-hosted-commit-terms-20270517.pdf (DocuSign-ready)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sigma — hosted commit proposal (approval request)

Marcus — quick ask: Rajiv is comfortable moving forward if we can confirm two things: the burst-pocket overage will be discounted to 0.6x standard overage, and we can accept the 3-month ramp for the commit step (they want to avoid an immediate billing cliff).

We'd like to approve a deal-level concession: 8% net effective discount on the incremental commit for the first 6 months (applied as a credit), plus the burst-pocket rate at 0.6x. That keeps list pricing intact but gives them the economics they need to commit.

Business case in brief:
- Annualized ARR upside if they commit now and expand into dedicated later (~$420k ARR uplift).
- Minimal immediate margin hit thanks to the ramp and credit structure.

Can you confirm sign-off so we can send the DocuSign envelope? Slack or quick reply is fine.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Dylan — this looks good overall. A couple of small asks before procurement signs:  

1) Can the burst-pocket be applied as a rolling monthly buffer rather than a hard one-off bucket? We run variable daily spikes and rolling buffer maps better to our usage patterns.
2) Please include the explicit per-minute token ceilings (we need the numbers for our gateway team).

If you can update the MAP to show the rolling burst behavior and drop the explicit ceilings in the SOW, we can route to signature this week. We'll have procurement pull the DocuSign link.

Thanks — we'll proceed after those two changes.
